zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Sharḥ
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿ألَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ﴾ ("did We not expand for you your breast?"): that is, We expanded it for Islam.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ﴾ ("and We removed from you your burden"): that is, We removed from you your sin, in that Allah forgave you your former and later sins.

zajjaj:3-4.t: ﴿الَّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ﴾ ﴿وَرَفَعْنا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ﴾ ("which weighed down your back, and We raised high your mention"): He made the mention of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ joined with the mention of Allah's oneness in the call to prayer, and in much of that in which Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, is mentioned, where one says: ”أشْهَدُ أنْ لا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ، أشْهَدَ أنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ“ ("I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah").

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying: ﴿فَإنَّ مَعَ العُسْرِ يُسْرًا﴾ ("for with hardship comes ease"): He mentioned "the hardship" with the alif and lām, then repeated its mention, so the meaning became: "with the hardship are two eases". And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: «”لا يَغْلِبُ عُسْرٌ يُسْرَيْنِ“» ("one hardship will not overcome two eases"); and it was said: «”لَوْ دَخَلَ العُسْرُ جُحْرًا لَدَخَلَ اليُسْرُ عَلَيْهِ“» ("if hardship entered a burrow, ease would enter in upon it"). That is because the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ were in severe straits, so Allah let them know that they would become well off and that [victories] would be opened to them, and He exchanged for them hardship with ease.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿وَإلى رَبِّكَ فارْغَبْ﴾ ("and to your Lord direct your longing"): that is, make your longing toward Allah alone.
